rationale.conceptual: The paper uses a custom finite-element/finite-difference scheme to solve coupled PDEs (3)-(4) with a non-standard eigenvalue identification (replace RHS with random functions, scan β, detect norm peaks). This requires genuine understanding of vectorial Maxwell equations, thermal stress modeling, and photoelasticity, plus careful numerical implementation to correctly locate propagation constants. It is not a standard library call; it is a multi-component method unique to this work.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has several sequential computation stages: thermal stress field, stress-modified index, PDE eigenvalue scan at multiple temperatures/wavelengths, and final B/τ calculation. These steps have dependencies and require careful numerical handling, but the orchestration is contained within a single Python script without complex external data acquisition or tooling. It fits a 4–6 stage pipeline typical of a computational physics paper.
